desc: Derive the counting formula: for middle index i with value v, count ways to pick 2 left + 2 right indices such that v's total (1+k) strictly exceeds every other value's frequency.
Case k=0: all four outer values pairwise distinct and ≠ v; count = DLp·DRp − (E²−Q)/2.
Case k=1: exactly one outer pick equals v; flv·(Lp·DRp − (Rp·E − U)) + frv·(Rp·DLp − (Lp·E − W)).
Case k=2: v appears 3×, always valid; sum over the four splits of the two v's across sides.
Derive and verify the exact formulas for k=0, k=1 (both orientations), k=2 contributions, testing against brute force on small random arrays.
Stress-test the full current solution implementation against brute force on random arrays (n ≤ 12, small alphabets) and verify the three provided examples; confirm final code correctness.
